why: Quantum-boundary and Euclidean-gradient values were loaded as typed FieldParamRecords but had no declared binding to runtime edges, so nothing could consume them and any consumer would have had to guess. docs/GRADIENT-FIELD-ALGEBRA.md already fixes the answer: a potential-derived edge quantity is an exact difference (FIELD_EDGE_DELTA), every field contract declares phase_policy: none, and a field measurement cannot authorize a phase crossing or a FoldGraph B transition.

binding.nature: exact difference, not a derivative: reversing the edge negates it exactly

separate_quantities.law: arc_weight and a potential difference are different quantities; neither may be substituted for the other

arc_weight.structure: a similarity on the cyclic phase graph, not a potential

separate_quantities.enforced_by: FieldMeasurementTable exposes no weight, no orientation and no authorization surface, and the lane proves W_E / O_E / admission are unchanged after binding

authority.registry_invariant_meaning: A27: XOR and gradient are both measurements; A28: a field measurement cannot authorize a phase crossing or a FoldGraph B transition

conservation.law: for a potential-derived field the integral between two points depends only on the endpoints, so every closed path sums to zero
conservation.endpoint_agreement: two different paths between the same endpoints agree and equal Phi(end) - Phi(start)
conservation.non_conservative_detection: a field whose declared curl is non-zero is reported is_conservative=false; the table never claims conservation it cannot prove

invariants.FB1: an edge measurement is the exact difference Phi(to) - Phi(from) over the typed record values, never a derivative and never a zero-filled default
invariants.FB2: reversing an edge negates the measurement exactly
invariants.FB3: every closed path over a conservative field sums to zero within 1e-9, and two paths between the same endpoints agree
invariants.FB4: a field whose declared curl is non-zero is marked non-conservative; conservation is never asserted on its behalf
invariants.FB5: binding measurements never writes an edge weight, an edge orientation, or an admission decision
invariants.FB6: a field measurement authorizes nothing: phase_policy is none and the table exposes no authorization surface
invariants.FB7: an unknown edge, a missing potential axis or a non-finite value is a typed refusal, not an empty measurement
